message.content:
**Famous American Composers (across a range of styles)**  

| Composer | Era / Genre | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Classical & popular (Broadway, jazz) | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, many Broadway hits |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Classical (20th‑century) | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *El Salón México* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical & musical theatre | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film music | Scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Classical | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Early modernist | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Contemporary classical | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| **Bobby McFerrin** (born 1950) | Vocal jazz, contemporary | *Don't Worry, Be Happy*, *The Art of the Song* |
| **Duke Ellington** (1899‑1974) | Jazz | *Mood Indigo*, *Take the A Train*, *Satin Doll* |
| **Miles Davis** (1926‑1991) | Jazz | *Kind of Blue*, *Bitches Brew*, *Sketches of Spain* |
| **Herbie Hancock** (born 1940) | Jazz, funk | *Head Hunters*, *Maiden Voyage*, *Rockit* |
| **Bob Dylan** (born 1941) | Folk, rock | *Blowin' in the Wind*, *Like a Rolling Stone*, *The Times They Are a-Changin'* |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** (1770‑1827) | Classical (German) | *Symphony No. 9*, *Moonlight Sonata* (not American but often studied in the U.S.) |

> **Why this list?**  
> The United States has produced a wide spectrum of composers—from early 20th‑century pioneers like Ives and Copland to contemporary film composers such as John Williams. Jazz giants like Duke Ellington and Miles Davis shaped not only American music but also global musical culture. In the realm of minimalism, Philip Glass and Steve Reich have become household names among contemporary classical audiences.  

> **How to use this list**  
> - If you’re looking for a composer whose work is frequently performed in concert halls, consider Copland, Barber, or Ives.  
> - For film music, John Williams is the most iconic, followed by composers like Hans Zimmer (though German, he works extensively in the U.S.).  
> - If you’re interested in jazz, start with Ellington, Davis, and Hancock.  
> - For contemporary classical or minimalist music, explore Glass, Reich, and Adams.  

Feel free to ask for more details on any of these composers or for recommendations on recordings, scores, or historical context!
